1.why: All eight screens are static cards with no animations, carousels or modal pop-ups, though the always-visible dark 'Logs' console adds technical clutter to an otherwise clean layout.

2.why: Each screen has a large bold heading and a single filled blue primary button (e.g. 'Verify code', 'Accept conditions'), so the key element is visually dominant, but the equally sized 'Logs' card competes for attention.

3.why: Each step presents one main task, but the recovery code must be located inside a developer-style 'Logs' console (step 2/3), which is not where a patient would expect to find what she needs.

4.why: The flow spans eight steps and requires transferring a 40-character token ('o79yOR_4yA5k0o9Hr0nEmlbxJ6sMB6UKc2sH-Cc9N0k'), a six-digit MFA code, and remembering a 12-character password rule set.

5.why: No 'remember me' checkbox, autofill hint, password-manager suggestion or 'show password' toggle appears on any screen, including the login/recovery and new-password pages.

6.why: Nothing is saved or pre-recognised for the user — the email must be typed from scratch and the only 'familiar item' offered is an opaque random token in a console log.

7.why: Body text is short, plain-language and in a legible sans-serif at good size (e.g. 'Choose at least 12 characters with uppercase, lowercase, a number, and a symbol.'), though log text is small monospace.

8.why: No error state is shown in any of the eight screenshots — only success/neutral notices — so there is no observable evidence of error messages that explain a problem and its fix.

9.why: Requirements are stated in prose but no worked examples or field placeholders are provided; the step-01 email field is empty with no sample format, and no example password is shown.

10.why: The steps that do offer options label them plainly ('Open simulated verification link' vs 'Enter recovery code'), but there is only one authentication path and no visible password/code/face-login choice.

11.why: Every screen presents a single primary action with at most one secondary option ('Start over'), so the user is never faced with many simultaneous choices.

12.why: Outcomes are explicitly confirmed after each action — 'a recovery message has been prepared', 'Mock MFA verification completed', 'Appointment request received' — mirrored in the log panel.

13.why: Each new step carries a one-line instruction plus safety tips ('Stay safe: Hospital staff will never ask for your password…', 'Do not share passwords, recovery links, or security codes').

14.why: 'Start over' exists on the code-verification screen and 'Return to recovery start' at the end, but the password, MFA and privacy screens offer no back or retry control.

15.why: All screens reuse the identical dark-blue header, white rounded card, bold heading, label-above-field inputs and blue primary button, making the pattern highly predictable.
